## Context / Problem
With `timeout_method = "thread"` (pyproject `[tool.pytest.ini_options]`), a test that exceeds its pytest-timeout budget under xdist does not report `Failed: Timeout`. pytest-timeout's watchdog thread calls `os._exit(1)` in the worker, the controller sees `[gwN] node down: Not properly terminated`, the crash guard (`tests/_crash_guard.py`) prints `xdist worker=gwN terminated abnormally: Not properly terminated`, and the test is FAILED with no traceback, no stack dump, and no indication that a timeout fired. Every such incident starts as a mystery crash investigation (e.g. uneducated-conveyable-nabarlek, subjective-forgeable-banteng, albinic-agrologic-dolphin, skipping-unamorous-massasauga).

## Reproduction (current main a8cf8fffc2a)
`env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest -p no:cacheprovider -n 2 -o timeout=20 tests/unit/test_opcert_key_copy_leak_tortoise.py` -> `[gw0] node down: Not properly terminated`, `worker 'gw0' crashed while running ...test_signer_test_modules_leave_no_key_copy_in_the_temp_dir`, `1 failed, 5 passed`, and no `Timeout` text anywhere in the output.

## Approach
Not yet planned. A fix must keep the thread method (test_timeout_budget_headroom.py pins it because signal mode cannot fire inside a blocking C call) and make a timeout kill name itself as a timeout, with the test id, in the controller's output.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Under xdist, a test that exceeds its pytest-timeout budget is reported in the controller output as a timeout naming the test id, not only as `Not properly terminated`.
- [ ] A test reproduces the silent-crash shape and fails before the fix.
compiled_state.title: xdist timeout kills report as silent worker crashes
